posts.mainText: White House released National AI Legislative Framework on March 20, 2026, urging Congress to enact federal AI laws preempting state regulations on frontier models and child safety.
posts.replyText: Promotes unified federal coordination over fragmented state efforts but challenges state legitimacy and innovation in AI safety rules.

posts.mainText: New Jersey Assembly passed bill requiring large data centers, including AI facilities, to fund their grid upgrades amid surging electricity demands.
posts.replyText: Strengthens institutional coordination between utilities and AI infrastructure, enhancing legitimacy by addressing public energy cost concerns tied to AI growth.

posts.mainText: Reps. Ocasio-Cortez and Sanders introduced federal bill for moratorium on new AI data centers to curb grid strain and rising energy costs.
posts.replyText: Pushes cross-party federal oversight on AI infrastructure, fostering coordination on safety externalities like energy security and public legitimacy.

posts.mainText: East China Normal University study warns AI revives ideological competition, reshaping political legitimacy through liberal vs authoritarian algorithmic governance models.
posts.replyText: Highlights need for global coordination on AI's impact on national power and trust, urging legitimacy via oversight like algorithmic constitutionalism.

posts.mainText: Analyses praise California's Q1 laws: SB 53 mandates frontier AI risk disclosures; SB 243 sets chatbot safety rules; AB 2013 requires training data transparency.
posts.replyText: State-level advances fill federal gaps, boosting developer accountability and coordination for AI safety amid national framework debates.
